problem.en: Prepare the BRS of Rao & Co. as on 31 March 2025. Cash book (Dr) ₹25,000. Cheques issued not presented ₹6,000; cheques deposited not credited ₹4,500; bank charges ₹200; interest credited by bank ₹350; insurance premium paid by bank ₹1,200; dividend collected by bank ₹2,000.

steps.en: Add: cheques issued not presented 6,000 + interest credited 350 + dividend collected 2,000 = ₹8,350 → ₹33,350.
Less: cheques not credited 4,500 + bank charges 200 + insurance 1,200 = ₹5,900.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Prepare the BRS of Rao & Co. as on 31 March 2025. Cash book (Dr) ₹25,000. say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Prepare the BRS of Rao & Co. as on 31 March 2025. Cash book Dr 25,000 rupees. Cheques issued not presented 6,000 rupees; cheques deposited not credited 4,500 rupees; bank charges 200 rupees; interest credited by bank 350 rupees; insurance premium paid by bank 1,200 rupees; dividend collected by bank 2,000 rupees.
Balance as per cash book: 25,000 rupees.
Add: cheques issued not presented 6,000 plus interest credited 350 plus dividend collected 2,000 equals 8,350 rupees gives 33,350 rupees.
Less: cheques not credited 4,500 plus bank charges 200 plus insurance 1,200 equals 5,900 rupees.
Balance as per pass book equals 33,350 minus 5,900 equals 27,450 rupees.
So the answer is Balance as per pass book 27,450 rupees.

problem.en: Use the same data but start from the pass book balance of ₹27,450 to arrive at the cash book balance.

steps.en: Add: cheques not credited 4,500 + bank charges 200 + insurance 1,200 = ₹5,900 → ₹33,350.
Less: cheques not presented 6,000 + interest 350 + dividend 2,000 = ₹8,350.
Balance as per cash book = 33,350 − 8,350 = ₹25,000, which checks.
